newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian police end Greenpeace road protest.
newsitem.headline: Austrian police end Greenpeace road protest.

text.p: Austrian police cleared demonstrators from the main Tuaern Alpine highway into Germany on Wednesday, ending a Greenpeace protest against rising levels of traffic pollution, the pressure group said.
Police cut free around 80 activists who had chained themselves to both ends of a tunnel on the busy route between Salzburg and Munich in Germany, causing long tailbacks.
No one was hurt and there were no arrests.
Greenpeace vowed to continue its campaign until Austrian Economy Minister Johann Farnleiter agreed to consider its demands for higher road tolls across Austria.
"We will continue to take action against truck transit, especially before the EU elections on October 13", a Greenpeace spokesman told Reuters.
The route had seen heavy goods vehicle traffic rise 20 percent by day and 45 percent by night since February 1996, Greenpeace said. It argued that raising tolls was the only way to reduce traffic.
Austria is currently locked in a legal battle with the European Commission over the levels of tolls on the Brenner Alpine route in the southern Tyrol region.
Austria has been accused of breaching EU legislation by doubling the night toll for trucks to 2,300 schillings ($215) on the route through the Brenner Pass.

But Austria says the pass is an environmentally-sensitive area which must be protected against increasing traffic, in particular from trucks and tourist vehicles which cut through the pass between Germany and Italy.
